articles.title: At least 11 killed as Russia launches ‘massive’ attack on Ukraine
articles.body:
At least 20 killed as Russia launches ‘massive’ attack on Ukraine
Ukraine’s air force says Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles in overnight attack.
At least 20 people, including children, have been killed as Russia launched a barrage of drones and missiles across Ukraine, according to Ukrainian authorities.
Ukraine’s air force said on Wednesday that Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles, and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles in the overnight attack. It added air defence units downed 161 targets.
Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, and Poltava in central Ukraine, the southeastern region of Dnipropetrovsk, and Kharkiv in the northeast were the focus of the Russian attacks, authorities said.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a social media post that Russia had fired 70 missiles and also drones in one of its biggest attacks since Moscow launched the war in 2022.
“One of the key targets was our energy infrastructure. The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” Zelenskyy said.
The attacks also damaged residential buildings, industrial facilities, and infrastructure, according to Ukrainian officials.
In Pryluki, in the northern Chernihiv region, a Russian missile slammed into a five-storey residential building, regional authorities said. At least 14 people, including four children, were killed and 50 others wounded, emergency services said.
Kyiv’s Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were killed in the densely populated Darnytskyi neighbourhood in a fire caused by an air attack.
Two people were killed when missiles hit high-rise buildings in Dnipro and Kremenchuk in central Ukraine, while two others died in Oleksandriya, Zelenskyy said.
‘Massive’ attack
Russia’s Ministry of Defence said its forces carried out a “massive strike” on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea-, and air-launched weapons, as well as drones.
Targets included sites where the company Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv, as well as in the regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, and Kharkiv, it said.
The attacks also targeted port and ship-repair infrastructure in the Odesa region, as well as vessels it said were being used in the interests of Ukraine’s armed forces, the ministry added.
“Ukraine has once again been hit by Russian missiles throughout the night,” Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine’s parliamentary commissioner for human rights, said on Telegram.
“Another sleepless night, another act of terror, after which people still have to plan their working day despite everything,” he added.
Kyiv has come under relentless bombardment in recent weeks, with Russian air attacks on energy infrastructure, rail and road transport, including the bridges that connect the city over the Dnipro River.
Air raid sirens have sounded almost constantly, urging residents to take cover in basements, shelters and subway stations.
In a separate post, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces hit four Russian targets over the last 24 hours, including two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara, and Astrakhan regions, as well as carrying out a response in the Black Sea.
He called the attacks a “just” response to Moscow’s strikes, and added that the facilities hit helped “Russia finance and wage its brutal war”.
Concerns over Black Sea navigation
As the war intensifies and expands, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has pressed Russian President Putin to ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea.
A statement by the Turkish presidency said Erdogan reiterated his offer to help facilitate direct talks between Russia and Ukraine, saying that safe Black Sea access was important to Ankara.
The conversation between the Turkish and Russian leaders came after drones hit two commercial vessels early on Tuesday as attacks on Black Sea shipping increase amid an intensifying Russia-Ukraine war. One vessel caught fire, while the other sank.
Bulgarian authorities say they have ended search operations after confirming that no survivors were found from the ship that sank off the country’s coast.

articles.title: Expert on Fox News: Russian Geran-4 Drone Likely Used in Black Sea Ship Attack
articles.body:
Bulgaria Falls to 90th in World Football Rankings
Bulgaria has fallen five places to 90th in the latest FIFA world rankings, with the decline following a poor start to the Nations League campaign
A suspected coordinated attack by aerial and maritime drones on two commercial vessels inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone was likely carried out using a Russian Geran-4 drone, drone manufacturer Draganfly founder Cameron Chell told Fox News, as one ship sank and its crew members remain missing.
The second vessel suffered heavy damage and caught fire in the attack, which took place Tuesday about 70 nautical miles off the eastern Bulgarian coastal town of Byala. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky blamed Russia and subsequently warned that Moscow was preparing for a new "massive strike."
Chell said the precision strikes could signal a dangerous escalation and possibly preparations for broader Russian military operations.
"They likely used a 'Geran-4' aerial drone to disable the ship, or the 'Maran' surface vessel," Chell told Fox News about the first attack. He explained that the Geran generally approaches its target at a very steep angle during the final stage, suggesting that an aerial drone alone was unlikely to have been responsible for the strike.
He said only a limited number of precision drones can travel immediately above the sea, which would be required to deliver a blow capable of sinking a vessel rapidly.
"The nature of this attack suggests a combination of aerial and surface-based strikes," Chell said.
The strikes occurred inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, extending the conflict into the economic waters of a NATO member state.
Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence and security agencies were investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
"Our intelligence and special services are currently working to gather all available information regarding this latest Black Sea attack on civilian vessels," he wrote on X.
"Our naval forces have contacted their Bulgarian counterparts, and it has been determined that this was a combined Russian attack involving both sea and aerial drones."
Chell said the location and mixed nature of the attacks could fit Russia’s objective of generating additional instability in the region.
"We see the scale of the geopolitical chaos being created, and a situation like this works to Russia's advantage in the region," he said.
He said the deployment of different types of assets makes it harder to distinguish conventional military operations and reflects an expansion in strategy and tactics.
"This indicates a broader military posture that Russia appears to be adopting, as well as a genuine desire, at least on the surface, to escalate the situation," Chell stated.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev also confirmed that aerial and maritime drones had struck two commercial vessels traveling along shipping routes inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. He characterized the incident as a "flagrant and blatant violation of international law."
The British maritime risk company Vanguard identified the vessel that sank as the cargo ship Alfa Watan. It suffered severe structural damage before going down and was carrying an unspecified cargo, while the size of its crew was not known.
The nearby Bulgarian ferry DIOSCURIA moved toward the location after its crew saw an explosion and received distress calls.
Rescuers found an overturned lifeboat, life rafts and life jackets among the wreckage.
The Navy, Air Force and Border Police launched a search and rescue operation for the missing crew members while also monitoring possible environmental risks.
Chell said the apparent synchronization of the attacks was especially significant.
"Not only is highly sophisticated equipment being used, but it is being used in a coordinated manner," he said.
"These two ships were traveling in opposite directions. One had just set off after leaving Ukraine the previous day," Chell added.
"These actions were coordinated, and both ships were struck at approximately the same time. This reveals yet another level of coordination," the expert said.
Vanguard identified the second vessel as the cargo ship ABLE, which was carrying grain and caught fire after being hit. The crew of a Bulgarian ferry evacuated all 18 sailors aboard, including 11 Turkish nationals and seven Indian nationals.
Two members of the crew suffered serious injuries and were transported by air to a medical facility in Varna. The other 16 people were brought safely ashore.
Radev called an emergency government meeting after the attacks. He stressed that it was still unclear whether Russia or Ukraine had launched the drones, while warning that the war was expanding in scale.
"Such an attack in the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable," Radev told journalists.
"If this war is not brought to an end in time, it will continue to expand its geographical scope and increase the risk of a global conflict."
Chell said the strikes inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone could interfere with a major maritime corridor and increase concerns among commercial shipping operators.
"All this creates an almost ideal scenario for the Russians to sow chaos there, not only to disrupt the economic maritime corridor in the region but, specifically, the one that is vital for Ukraine," he said.
He compared Russia’s approach with that of Iran, saying Tehran had generated sufficient uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz to discourage operators from risking passage by their ships.
The attacks occurred as assaults against commercial shipping in the Black Sea become more frequent. On Monday, two people were killed after a ship caught fire off the Romanian coast.
Ambrey, a British company specializing in global maritime risk assessment, reported more than 210 attacks against commercial vessels from July through the end of September.

The search for the crew of the sunken cargo ship ALFA WATAN has been terminated and will not resume, the Bulgarian Maritime Search and Rescue Center announced

articles.title: 14 dead in Pryluky, two each in Kyiv, Kremenchuk, and Oleksandriia: Russia’s night of 70 missiles
articles.body:
Russia attacked Kyiv and 12 oblasts overnight on 7 October with about 70 missiles, many of them ballistic, as well as Shahed drones, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The strikes killed at least 20 people, with the deadliest hit on an apartment block in Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast. Russia also hit Kremenchuk, Oleksandriia, Dnipro, and Zaporizhzhia, while Poland scrambled its jets.
Moscow has likely begun its winter strike campaign earlier than usual, aiming to make civilian life in Ukraine unbearable, and UN figures already show civilian casualties running 55% above last year's.
Update: Pryluky death toll rises to 14, including four children
The death toll from the Russian strike on Pryluky has risen to 14, including four children, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said on the afternoon of 7 October. Fifty people were injured, seven of them children, and rescuers pulled 15 people from the rubble, including a child.
Russia attacked Pryluky with cruise missiles, and one scored a direct hit on the five-story apartment building, Chernihiv Oblast head Viacheslav Chaus said. Earlier in the day, he reported that 27 of the injured had been hospitalized, three in serious condition. The search-and-rescue operation was still under way.
Morning repoting: five dead in Pryluky
A Russian missile struck a five-story apartment building in Pryluky early in the morning, while residents were still asleep, Chernihiv Oblast head Viacheslav Chaus said. The strike completely destroyed one sectkion of the building, killing five people and injuring 26, including five children, Ukraine's National Police reported. Rescuers pulled three people from the rubble, including a child, and more people may still be trapped, Chaus said.
"Today, for Putin's birthday, the Russian army 'gave' him the destruction of an apartment building in Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast. It was an ordinary five-story building," Zelenskyy said.
Kyiv, Kremenchuk, and Oleksandriia
In Kyiv, Russian missiles hit non-residential buildings and warehouses in the Obolonskyi and Podilskyi districts, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Strikes also hit the Shevchenkivskyi district, and debris burned in the Darnytskyi district, he added. In the Darnytskyi district, a missile set fire to a garage cooperative, where firefighters rescued two people and found two men dead, Klitschko wrote. Police and rescuers worked to defuse an unexploded ballistic missile that fell among apartment blocks in the same district, the National Police said.
In Kremenchuk, Russian missiles hit a densely populated residential area, killing two people and injuring seven, Poltava Oblast head Vitalii Diakivnych said. Zelenskyy later put the number of injured at eight and said four high-rises were damaged.
In Oleksandriia in Kirovohrad Oblast, Russia hit an enterprise. One person was killed, three injured, and two were out of contact, Kirovohrad Oblast head Andrii Raikovych said. Zelenskyy later put the death toll there at two.
Drones and other targets
In Dnipro, Russian strikes damaged an industrial enterprise, apartment buildings, and a sports club, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast head Oleksandr Hanzha said. In Nikopol district, the attacks injured a 65-year-old woman and a 64-year-old man. Russia also struck Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast with a missile, and a drone hit an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, police said.
In Zaporizhzhia, Russia attacked a transport infrastructure facility, acting oblast head Mykhailo Semikin said, a day after a strike on one of the city's bridges over the Dnipro halted traffic. In Kyiv Oblast, three production and warehouse buildings were damaged in Obukhiv district, with no casualties, the Kyiv Oblast Military Administration said.
Air defense downed five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles, and 117 drones, while missiles and drones hit 18 locations, the Air Force said. Polish military aircraft took off and Poland put its ground-based air defense on alert during the attack, Poland's Operational Command said.
Russian ballistic missiles remain the biggest challenge, Zelenskyy said, adding that Ukraine is searching daily for Patriot missiles.
Strikes across the front over the past day
Russian attacks killed one person and injured 11 in Kherson Oblast over the past day, the Kherson Oblast Military Administration reported. Russia injured 12 people in Donetsk Oblast on 6 October, Donetsk Oblast head Vadym Filashkin said. Two people were injured in Kharkiv Oblast, Kharkiv Oblast head Oleh Syniehubov said.
Bridges and a maternity hospital in Russia's sights
Russia has stepped up strikes on Kyiv's bridges and has now extended them to Zaporizhzhia. In September, a Russian ballistic and hypersonic missile attack on Kyiv damaged a maternity hospital.

articles.title: Zelensky: Russia ‘Gifted’ Putin an Attack Killing 5 in Pryluky
articles.body:
Russia launched 70 missiles and attack drones across Ukraine on Wednesday, Oct. 7 – Russian President Vladimir Putin’s birthday – striking residential buildings and energy infrastructure and killing at least 20 civilians.
The deadliest strike destroyed an ordinary five-story apartment building in Pryluky, Chernihiv region. The death toll there has risen to 14, including four children, while 50 people were injured, seven of them children, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS).
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Rescuers pulled 15 people alive from the destroyed building, including one child.
President Volodymyr Zelensky described the destruction as a “gift” from the Russian military to Putin on his birthday.
“Today, on Putin’s birthday, the Russian army ‘gifted’ him the destruction of a residential building in Pryluky,” Zelensky wrote on Telegram.
“This was an ordinary five-story apartment building,” he added.
Four children among 14 killed in Pryluky
The DSNS initially reported five deaths and 26 injuries in Pryluky. As rescuers searched the wreckage, the number of confirmed casualties continued to rise.
The latest update put the toll at 14 dead and 50 injured. Four children were among those killed, while seven children were injured.
Emergency crews rescued 15 people from the damaged building, including one child.
The DSNS did not immediately disclose the ages of the children killed or provide details about the conditions of those wounded.
Russian Attack Leaves Unexploded Ballistic Missile Among Homes in Kyiv, Hits Film Studio and Bird Center
Homes damaged across Ukraine
The strike on Pryluky formed part of a nationwide Russian barrage that targeted infrastructure in Kyiv and 12 Ukrainian regions.
Five apartment buildings were damaged in Dnipro, while four high-rises were struck in Kremenchuk. Two people were killed and eight injured in the attacks affecting the two cities, according to Zelensky.
A Russian drone damaged another apartment building in Zaporizhzhia.
Russian forces also killed two people in Kyiv and another two in Oleksandriia, Kirovohrad region.
Combined with the updated toll in Pryluky, the figures announced by Ukrainian authorities indicate that at least 20 people were killed across the country.
Zelensky offered his condolences to the families of those killed.
Multiple explosions rocked Kyiv early Wednesday, hours after Zelensky warned that Ukrainian intelligence had obtained information about Russian preparations for a massive attack.
Damage was reported in the capital’s Obolonskyi, Podilskyi, Darnytskyi, and Shevchenkivskyi districts. Warehouses and other non-residential facilities were among the sites hit.
Russia fires 70 missiles
Zelensky said Russia launched 70 missiles, including a significant number of ballistic weapons, as well as Shahed-type attack drones.
Ukrainian air defenses intercepted only part of the barrage.
“This was one of the most treacherous strikes,” Zelensky said. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively.”
One of the principal targets was Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as Russia intensifies attacks on the country’s power system ahead of the winter season.
The president did not specify how many of the 70 missiles were intercepted or provide a breakdown of the weapons used.
Zelensky renews Patriot appeal
Zelensky described Russian ballistic missiles as Ukraine’s greatest current air defense challenge.
Ukraine relies primarily on US-made Patriot systems to intercept Russian ballistic missiles, but Kyiv has repeatedly warned that it lacks sufficient launchers and interceptor missiles to protect its cities and critical infrastructure.
“Air defense packages are now a vital necessity for us,” Zelensky said.
“That is why we search every day for missiles for the Patriots, which can and must genuinely protect people’s lives here, in Ukrainian skies.”

articles.title: At least 11 dead, 34 injured after ‘vile’ attack on Ukraine on Putin’s birthday, Zelenskyy says – Europe live
articles.body:
French interior minister rejects allegation of heavy-handed police response to student protests
French interior minister Laurent Nuñez rejected allegations of police brutality in their response to on-going French student protests, saying officers only intervene when there is damage or violence.
Addressing French lawmakers, he said the protest movement was “unprecedented” because of “very serious violence,” franceinfo reported.
French interior minister Laurent Nuñez rejected allegations of police brutality in their response to on-going student protests, saying officers only intervene when there is damage or violence. Addressing French lawmakers, he said the protest movement was “unprecedented” because of “very serious violence,” Nuñez said a total of 6,629 people have been arrested since the protests began. Meanwhile, 761 police officers and gendarmes have been injured, alongside 215 students and 89 members of teaching staff.
France PM Sébastien Lecornu listed five key areas the government will address: replacing absent teachers, improving school facilities, organising the school day, and revising Parcoursup, France’s web portal and pre-enrolment platform, to make it more user-friendly. He added the government’s initial decisions “will be presented at the end of October.” On the protests, he said: “The police have not been instructed to confront high school students.”
A new Elabe poll for BFMTV shows that 55% of French people support the high school protests. While 35% oppose the movement, 10% say they have no clear view.
US secretary of state Marco Rubio called for the nations of the West to return to their civilizational roots and restore the values that drove the rise of Europe and North America to global dominance for centuries in a speech in Athens.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia’s military of deliberately killing civilians and bombing residential buildings as a macabre gift for Vladimir Putin, who celebrates his 74th birthday on Wednesday. Ukraine’s president described Russia’s overnight drone and missiles strikes, which killed at least 24 people, as “despicable”. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” he said.
A knife attack at a vocational school in Ostrołęka, Poland left at least seven people injured, including two seriously, as reported by Poland’s RMF FM radio.
On the government pledging to review the demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October on issues ranging from renovating buildings to make more teachers available, Lecornu said: “In the past, too many promises were not kept, quite simply because they were untenable.
“What I want are concrete, quick and fully funded answers.”
Lecornu also confirmed that France will release 10 million barrels of diesel from its strategic stocks to try to ease tight supplies amid surging energy prices stemming from the wars in Iran and in Ukraine.
He said: “Last Friday, President (Emmanuel) Macron convened an emergency meeting of the G7, which decided to mobilize strategic reserves in a coordinated manner. As part of this effort, we will make 10 million barrels of diesel from our reserves available to distributors in France.”
Lecornu said the move “will automatically lower prices at the pump by an estimated amount ranging from 0.12 to 0.18 euros per liter of diesel.”
Government to present school proposals by end of this month, says Lecornu
Lecornu listed five key areas the government will address: replacing absent teachers, improving school facilities, organising the school day, and revising Parcoursup, France’s web portal and pre-enrolment platform, to make it more user-friendly.
He added the government’s initial decisions “will be presented at the end of October.”
Lecornu added the dialogue sessions that began in high schools on Wednesday are to continue “starting tomorrow, in each high school, and until next week.”
'Police not instructed to confront students,' says Lecornu
France PM Sébastien Lecornu has begun his address by discussing the high school student protests, Liberation reported. He said: “The police have not been instructed to confront high school students.”
A formal arrest warrant has been issued against Germany’s former top spy, with a judge ordering him to be held in pre-trial detention a day after he was arrested on suspicion of treason and spying on behalf of an overseas intelligence agency.
August Hanning, 80, is accused of buying secret documents from a former colleague and using them to advise a foreign intelligence service, according to the country’s office of the federal prosecutor.
Wednesday’s formal arrest warrant followed Hanning’s arrest on Tuesday, along with that of his former office head, Manfred D. It has sent shock waves through Germany’s political and intelligence community, with analysts calling it potentially the country’s biggest espionage scandal since the end of the cold war.
A lawyer for Hanning denied he had been involved in any wrongdoing on Wednesday, telling the conservative daily newspaper Die Welt: “While it is true that he was in possession of confidential documents, the allegation that he passed on information contained therein to the detriment of Germany, let alone for payment, is incorrect.”
West should 'learn from the men of Ancient Greece', says Rubio in Athens speech
US secretary of state Marco Rubio called for the nations of the West to return to their civilizational roots and restore the values that drove the rise of Europe and North America to global dominance for centuries in a speech in Athens.
Rubio said: “It has become fashionable today to believe that enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the ‘global community’ over one’s own people. And I think here, too, we have much more to learn from the men of Ancient Greece. They knew that there was nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation, nor anything selfish or wrong about fighting to defend its interests above all else.”
Rubio also urged Europe to uphold its traditional values.
“Today, we find ourselves at a crossroads.
“The next decade will write the story of the next century. The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world, or resigns itself to a future of atrophy, and servitude, and decline. We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.”
France summoned Iran’s ambassador over what foreign ministry spokesperson Pascal Confavreux described as an Iranian disinformation campaign targeting France’s secondary school student protest movement.
The envoy was told of the “absolutely unacceptable” nature of false content disseminated online by official Iranian foreign ministry accounts, Confavreux said in a statement, adding that Tehran’s October 6 summons of the French ambassador was baseless.
“These undignified provocations must cease,” he said.
Iran on Tuesday summoned France’s envoy in Tehran over the ongoing student protests, accusing Paris of the “violent treatment” of demonstrators and of extensive human rights violations, according to Iranian state media.
Back to the protests in France and the administrative court has suspended the ban on gatherings around 45 schools in Haute-Garonne, Occitanie, seeing it as an attack on the freedom to demonstrate, BFMTV reported.
The ban “is neither appropriate nor proportionate and whose necessity is not established, constitutes a serious and manifestly illegal infringement of the freedom of demonstration and the freedom of assembly,” the administrative court of Toulouse said in its decision.
Russian missiles and drones struck Ukrainian cities including Kyiv, Pryluky and Kremenchuk overnight on Tuesday. Two people were killed in Kyiv, while a strike destroyed an apartment block in Pryluky, in Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region, killing at least nine people including three children.
Following the attack on a teacher in La Ciotat who was doused with gasoline during student protests, three 16-year-olds will appear before the Marseille juvenile court in February 2027, newspaper Liberation reported.
More from the Greek capital where visiting US Secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has been dominating the news.
In a day packed with talk of energy and defense, gas ‘corridors’ and trade, counterterrorism and US military bases - all earning Greece the encomium of being the region’s “pillar of stability” according to Rubio – it is the foreign policy chief, himself, who has made the news.
Rubio’s decision to use the trip to deliver a major address “on democracy and its future” from the ancient Pnyx has imbued the visit with an air of excitement.
Until last night it was far from sure that the US secretary of state would have access to the setting because of security reasons.
Only hours before more than 1,500 protestors, appalled by the war in Iran, had marched through the streets of central Athens waving banners declaring him persona non grata.
Excerpts of Rubio’s address released by the State department suggest he will focus on the shared values that have united Americans and Europeans in what has also been described as a rallying cry for “a great renewal of the Western spirit.”
But there are also fears the US secretary of state may use the setting to make a speech in the spirit of the blistering attack on Europe issued by Vice President JD Vance at the Munich Security conference last year. The speech is scheduled to take place in the next half hour.
Poll shows majority of French people supports high school protests, demands, but uncertain about their future
A new Elabe poll for BFMTV shows that 55% of French people support the high school protests.
While 35% oppose the movement, 10% say they have no clear view.
Support for the students’ demands is even higher, with 72% considering them legitimate – a view shared by majorities across the political spectrum, from left to right.
However, the public is far more divided over what should happen next: 55% believe students have made their point and should end the protests, while 27% think they should carry on.
'Impunity must end,' Le Pen says, as she offers her support to police over student protests
French far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen offered her strong support for the police, saying “impunity must end,” and “those who vandalise our schools, and their parents when they are minors, must pay for the damage they cause.”
“The French people should no longer have to finance the vandals,” she told reporters on a visit to Cournon-d’Auvergne.
She also said the police should have the support of the nation, and “not face constant accusations from those in power,” as she chose to use the protests to criticise the French president, Emmanuel Macron.
“While the far left spreads false accusations to stoke violence, Emmanuel Macron once again chooses to undermine those who protect the French people,” she said.
Le Pen leads the presidential polls ahead of next year’s election, with 33-34% of vote share in the first round, well ahead of Édouard Philippe and Jean-Luc Mélenchon at around 16-18%.

articles.title: Iranian strikes forced US troops to ‘abandon’ Kuwait base – CBS (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Iranian strikes forced US troops to ‘abandon’ Kuwait base – CBS (VIDEO)
Iranian strikes forced US troops to effectively abandon a major military base in Kuwait during the opening stages of the US-Israeli war on Iran, according to newly released footage and accounts from American servicemen obtained by CBS News.
Videos shared by US soldiers in breach of the Pentagon’s strict media policy show several drones nosediving into Camp Buehring, a major US Army staging facility roughly 40km from the Iraqi border, as well as damage to buildings and military equipment. CBS said it authenticated the recordings using embedded metadata and imagery of the aftermath.
The installation came under repeated attack by Iranian ballistic missiles and drones after hostilities began on February 28. A US service member also told CBS that Iranian F-5 fighter jets flew missions against the base “so close to us I could see their helmets.”
Most of the roughly 7,000 troops stationed at Camp Buehring had already been dispersed before the war under what the Pentagon called its “get off the X” strategy, aimed at moving personnel away from fixed positions vulnerable to Iranian retaliation.
Some 100 soldiers, however, remained behind to defend the installation, where they were repeatedly forced into bunkers and ran critically low on ammunition, including Patriot interceptors.
“They hit us bad,” one serviceman told the outlet. “It was horrible... We had to abandon the base.”
The remaining troops eventually fled the base and established improvised forward operating outposts in the Kuwaiti desert, where they remained for weeks. No US personnel were killed, although several were injured, including two who were struck by lightning during desert sandstorms.
“CBKU got demolished,” the serviceman said. “They need to do an investigation. How come no one came to reinforce us?”
The Pentagon declined to comment directly on the CBS report, instead referring the outlet to remarks made by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in March, when he acknowledged that more than 90% of American personnel had been moved away from US regional bases.
The revelations come days after an Associated Press investigation raised separate questions about US preparations elsewhere in Kuwait. An Iranian drone struck an American operations center at Port Shuaiba on March 1, killing six soldiers and wounding dozens in what remains the deadliest known single attack on US troops during the conflict. Some of the wounded said troops initially treated each other with basic first-aid supplies and had to use Google to locate the nearest hospital in Kuwait City. The Pentagon has maintained that its medical response was appropriate.
The devastation at Camp Buehring was part of a much broader campaign against the US military footprint across the Middle East, with Iranian missiles and drones striking bases and installations in multiple countries and damaging aircraft, radar systems, hangars, barracks, and other infrastructure.
By September, CENTCOM said the war had already cost Washington $43.6 billion, a figure that did not include extensive damage to US bases across eight countries. The true personnel toll has also remained disputed: the Pentagon publicly listed 18 military deaths as of mid-September, while military sources cited by the Washington Post put the figure at 22 or 23.
As the damage mounted, the Pentagon tightened control over images emerging from the region. After an Iranian missile and drone strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on July 17 killed three US service members, CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper warned troops against filming strike sites, claiming that publicly posted footage was helping Tehran assess the accuracy and effects of its attacks. US allies hosting American bases have likewise imposed strict bans and penalties on filming military sites and strike aftermaths, making independent footage of Iranian attacks increasingly rare.

articles.title: Ukraine war latest: Russian attack on Pryluky kills at least 20, including 5 children
articles.body:
Ukraine war latest: Russian attack on Pryluky kills at least 20, including 5 children
Key developments on Oct. 7:
- Russia slams Ukraine with missiles, drones on Putin's 74th birthday, at least 26 dead including 5 children
- Huge blaze breaks out at Russian oil facility in Samara Oblast
- EU provides Ukraine 1.2 billion euros for drones and missiles
- Russia carried out sabotage against Danish defense firms, intelligence says
- Erdogan raises Black Sea safety in call with Putin
At least 26 people have been killed in yet another Russian overnight mass missile and drone attack on Ukrainian cities on Oct. 7, coinciding with Russian President Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday.
In the city of Pryluky, in Chernihiv Oblast, a Russian cruise missile hit a residential building, killing at least 20 people, including five children, and wounding at least 55, including seven children.
Three of the dead children, named Oleksandr, Kyrylo, and Serhiy, were only one year old, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a post on social media. The other child was an eight-year-old named Maksym, he added.
A fifth child was killed by the Russian strike, as Ukraine's state emergency service (DSNS) said as of 7:13 p.m. local time.
"Today, as a 'birthday gift' to Putin, the Russian army destroyed a residential building in Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region," Zelensky said.
"It was an ordinary five-story apartment block. There may still be people under the rubble. First responders are working nonstop at the site – doing everything possible to find every person," he added.
Chernihiv Oblast Governor Viacheslav Chaus said that on Putin's birthday, he hopes "the Russian dictator ends up in custody in The Hague or in hell."
"That is all he deserves."
Pryluky resident Halyna Osovyk, 55, woke up, and soon after, her flat was shaken by an explosion, she told the Kyiv Independent. Then came more strikes, smoke, and shattered windows. Across the road, two entrances of a neighboring apartment building were destroyed, and rescuers were searching the rubble for people.
The woman herself was still shaking as she spoke. Her hands and legs trembled.
"It was just sheer horror. And the sound of the missiles — you simply cannot put it into words," Osovyk said.
She knew some of those affected. One family was trapped under the debris – the mother, grandmother, and one child were killed, while another child was rescued and taken to the hospital. Another woman and her child were also pulled from the rubble and hospitalized, Osovyk said. As rescuers continued clearing the ruins, people waited for news of relatives who were still missing.
Pryluky had experienced Russian attacks before, she added, but never a morning like this. Asked what she would wish for Putin on his birthday, she replied: "I wish he could have what we are going through now."

Huge blaze breaks out at Russian oil facility in Samara Oblast
Large fires have broken out at a major oil pipeline and storage facility in Russia's Samara Oblast, according to footage shared on social media and NASA satellite monitoring.
Footage posted to social media showed large fires and clouds of black smoke above the facility, which is a major node in Russia's network of oil pipelines.
NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), which uses satellite data to detect thermal anomalies and fires, detected multiple hotspots at the facility.
The facility, which is located near the village of Prosvet, in Samara Oblast, includes pumping stations, tank farms, and blending stations. It has been a repeated target during Ukraine's campaign of deep strikes against Russian oil infrastructure.
Earlier that day, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alluded to a Ukrainian strike on oil facilities in Samara Oblast, without specifying which facility had been hit.
read also
EU provides Ukraine 1.2 billion euros for drones and missiles
The European Commission announced the disbursement of 1.24 billion euros ($1.4 billion) of defense support to Ukraine on Oct. 7, part of the bloc's 90 billion euro support loan ($100 billion) for Kyiv.
"Today's disbursement will help strengthen Ukraine's defense industry. And Ukraine's ability to defend itself. To protect people and infrastructure," said European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in a press statement.
"The money will be spent on drones, drone interceptors, drone ammunition, and missiles manufactured by Ukrainian entities," reads the press release.
The EU's 90 billion euro loan to Ukraine, approved in April 2026, was intended to provide two-thirds of Kyiv's financial and defense needs until the end of 2027.
In 2026, 28.3 billion euros ($31.7 billion) was earmarked for defense, and Ukraine's plans for how to spend that money have all been submitted and approved by Brussels.
read also
Russia carried out sabotage against Danish defense firms, intelligence says
Russia has stepped up efforts to disrupt Danish companies involved in supplying weapons to Ukraine, Denmark's intelligence service representative told Reuters on Oct. 7.
Josefine Christensen, an analyst at the Danish national security and intelligence service (PET), said Russia was increasingly focusing on targets directly connected to Western military support for Ukraine.
According to Christensen, Russia planned a lot of operations in spring but carried out "very little," while in early summer they started to carry out "a lot more."
She added that Russia's operational boldness is growing as it is now trying to hit targets that have a direct impact on the front line, meaning weapons production.
Russia is relying on individuals recruited online to conduct such operations. Some are first tasked with gathering information or photographing potential targets before being offered more serious assignments.
European drone manufacturers and suppliers have attracted particular attention. Christensen cited a list released by Russia's Defense Ministry in April that included European companies involved in producing drones and related components.
read also
Erdogan raises Black Sea safety in call with Putin
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 7, telling him Turkey is ready to contribute to efforts for direct talks between Russia and Ukraine, and stressing the importance of the safety of navigation in the Black Sea, according to Erdogan's office.
The two Presidents discussed bilateral relations, as well as regional and global issues, Turkey's Directorate of Communications said.
Erdogan also congratulated Putin on his birthday and his party's success in the latest Russian parliamentary elections, the office said.
The security situation for Black Sea shipping has worsened over the past weeks.
On Oct. 5, a cargo ship caught fire in the Black Sea off the Romanian coast after a Russian drone strike, killing two, injuring at least 11 more, and prompting a large search-and-rescue operation.
After Romanian media and authorities initially reported a fire on the grain ship Royad Mammadov, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that a civilian ship was attacked by two Russian drones, adding that it was a Turkish-owned ship transporting corn.
According to Zelensky, the ship was crewed by citizens of Azerbaijan and India. While the Russian strike killed the vessel's captain, Zelensky said. Romania's interior ministry said that two people were killed in the attack.

articles.title: Russian missile strike on apartment building in Ukraine kills 14, including four children. Zelensky calls it the Russian army’s ‘birthday gift’ to Putin.
articles.body:
Russian missile strike on apartment building in Ukraine kills 14, including four children. Zelensky calls it the Russian army’s ‘birthday gift’ to Putin.
Russia’s military carried out a combined missile and drone attack overnight and into the morning, striking several regions of Ukraine. Ukraine’s Air Force reported that air defenses had destroyed five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles, and 117 drones since the previous evening, including 38 jet-propelled drones.
In Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region, a cruise missile strike destroyed two sections of a five-story apartment building, according to data from authorities. Authorities said 14 people were killed, including four children, and 50 people, including seven children, were injured.
The strike also damaged other residential buildings in Pryluky, a children’s and youth creativity center, an industrial facility, and private vehicles.
In Kyiv, authorities reported several waves of ballistic missile strikes overnight. Two people were killed, and strikes hit four districts of the city.
Strikes on Kremenchuk killed two people. Authorities said a residential area there was hit.
“The Russian army’s ‘birthday present’ to Putin today was the destruction of an apartment building in Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, commenting on the strike. Vladimir Putin turned 74 on October 7.
Zelensky said the main target of the massive strike was energy infrastructure, adding that the Russians “wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively.”
Russia’s Defense Ministry said in its daily report that the strikes had targeted military facilities, including a drone assembly shop and a plant assembling the “Flamingo” missile in Kyiv, a factory producing unmanned boats in the Odesa region, and a shop producing drone components in the Kirovohrad region, among other facilities. The ministry did not report any strikes against energy infrastructure.
Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed that the target of the strike on Pryluky was an industrial facility that produces and stores components for “Flamingo” missiles.

articles.title: Kremlin responds to French ballistic missile launch
articles.body:
Kremlin responds to French ballistic missile launch
Russia views France’s nuclear-capable missile launch as a “loud and clear message” and will take “all necessary measures” to protect itself, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said.
The French military test-fired a submarine-launched M51.3 ballistic missile on Tuesday, in an exercise in the Atlantic Ocean watched by French President Emmanuel Macron. The weapon, a new variant of France’s 16-year-old M51 missile family, was launched without a warhead and splashed down in the North Atlantic, “hundreds of kilometres from any coastline,” according to the French military.
In a video message, Macron described the test as “a new demonstration of the credibility of our deterrence,” and “a clear message… for wherever it must be received.”
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Peskov said: “Problems should be resolved through dialogue, not demonstrative missile launches.”
“Europe has become obsessed with plans to militarize the European Union,” he continued. “This is bad because they are building their defense and security identity on confrontation with the Russian Federation. This is a dead end. As history has shown, this leads to nothing good.”
“Against the backdrop of such aggressive actions and such plans, Russia is on alert,” Peskov added. “We are taking all necessary measures to ensure our national security at the strategic level.”
Outside the US, France possesses NATO’s only independent nuclear arsenal, which Macron is currently modernizing and expanding. France plans to spend €7.4 billion ($8.3 billion) on nuclear deterrence in 2026, while its updated military program adds €36 billion to overall defense spending through 2030. Much of this money will be spent on multi-year submarine, missile, and warhead contracts, but a substantial sum will go toward Paris’ controversial “forward deterrence scheme.”
Under this scheme, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Sweden, and the UK will potentially host French nuclear weapons on a temporary basis and take part in French nuclear exercises.
Russia, which possesses the world’s largest nuclear arsenal, cannot view the deployment of atomic weapons on its borders “as anything other than a step toward escalating tensions,” Peskov said on Tuesday. Peskov was responding to the Lithuanian parliament’s vote to remove a constitutional ban on hosting nuclear weapons on its soil. Although Lithuania has not signed on to France’s “forward deterrence” plan, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas has expressed interest in hosting American nukes in Lithuania.

articles.title: Russia Fires Massive Missile-and-Drone Salvo at Ukraine, Leaving Dead and Damage Across Multiple Regions
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russia Fires Massive Missile-and-Drone Salvo at Ukraine, Leaving Dead and Damage Across Multiple Regions
Russia unleashed a massive overnight missile-and-drone barrage across Ukraine, killing at least 13 people and injuring 59—including three children—as a residential building was hit in Pryluky and an unexploded ballistic missile landed among homes in Kyiv.
Russia launched a large-scale combined missile and drone strike across Ukraine overnight into October 7, killing at least 13 people, damaging homes and industrial facilities, and leaving an unexploded ballistic missile embedded among residential buildings in Kyiv.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported damage across several districts of the capital. In the Darnytskyi district, a fire broke out at a garage complex following the strike.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Emergency crews rescued two people while fighting the blaze and later recovered the bodies of two others.
Elsewhere in Darnytskyi, Kyiv police and emergency specialists began a complex operation to neutralize an unexploded ballistic missile discovered among residential buildings. Explosives experts were working to remove its warhead before transporting it to a testing range for final disposal.
The wider Kyiv region was also targeted by both drones and ballistic missiles. In the Obukhiv district, three production and warehouse facilities were damaged and fires broke out, according to Kyiv regional administration head Tymur Tkachenko. A truck and trailer were also damaged, though no casualties were reported there.
“Overnight, the region came under a combined attack by enemy drones and ballistic missiles. In the Obukhiv district, three production and warehouse facilities were damaged. Fires broke out—they have now been contained,” Tkachenko said.
Ukraine’s Air Force said Russian forces began the barrage at around 6 pm on October 6, using a wide mix of long-range weapons.
The strike included Zircon and Onyx missiles launched from Russia’s Rostov region, Iskander-M, S-400 and North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles launched from the Bryansk and Voronezh regions, as well as 48 Kh-101, Iskander-K and Kalibr cruise missiles launched from air, ground and naval platforms.
Russia also launched 130 Shahed-type, Gerbera and Parodiya drones from several directions, including Russian territory, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea. Of those, 46 were jet-powered UAVs.
Ukraine’s Air Force reported neutralizing five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles and 117 drones during the overnight strike.
The main targets were the Kyiv, Kharkiv, Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk regions.
One of the deadliest strikes was recorded in Kremenchuk, Poltava region, where preliminary reports indicated that two people were killed and seven others wounded.
“According to preliminary information, two people were killed. My condolences to their families and loved ones. Seven more people were injured,” Poltava regional administration head Volodymyr Diakyvnych said.
The heaviest confirmed toll was reported in Pryluky, Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile struck a multi-story residential building.
UPD. The death toll in Pryluky rose as rescuers continued searching the ruins of the five-story apartment building. Emergency crews recovered the bodies of three children from beneath the rubble, bringing the number of people killed at the site to nine.
At least 50 people were injured in the strike. Twenty-three are being treated on an outpatient basis, while 27 were hospitalized, including three in serious condition. Rescuers have pulled 12 people alive from the damaged building.
Chernihiv regional administration head said five people were confirmed killed and at least 25 injured, warning that the number of victims could still rise as emergency crews continued clearing the rubble.
“At present, it is known that the missile strike on the multi-story building claimed the lives of five people. At least 25 people were injured. Unfortunately, the number of victims may be higher. The relevant services are working—clearing the rubble,” he said.
Three people were rescued from the damaged building, including a child.
Earlier, a Russian attack destroyed the KUSUM pharmaceutical plant in Sumy, killing one employee and halting production at the facility.
